confidence_note: Facts about Spartak Tennis Club (one indoor court, rundown, freezing climate, more top-20 women than the entire US in recent years, same warm-up for five-year-olds and a top-ten player, slow-motion swings and swings with no ball called imitatsiya, three years before competing, coach saying technique is everything) are taken from Coyle's own website post on Spartak; the book's appearance of Spartak is from memory, not verified in the text. The top-20 figure covers a few recent years only (secondary sources suggest the mid-2000s). Old TR text (Hungary chess, Dominican baseball, Jeju golf, Polgar family) not verified and dropped; Polgar and 'geniuses are made' quote not used. DB title is Turkish 'Yetenek Kodu'.
facts: Coyle came across Spartak while writing about talent hotbeds.
One rundown indoor court in a freezing climate.
Produced more top-20 women than the entire US in recent years.
Every player, from five-year-olds to a world top-ten player, starts with the same eye-hand warm-up of bouncing and catching.
Slow-motion swings and swings with no ball are called imitatsiya.
Players may compete only after three years of practice.
A Spartak coach: Technique is everything; starting without it is a 'Big, big mistake'.
opening_idea: The top-ten player does the beginner warm-up.

lessons.idea: Slow, small, repeated work builds technique.

reflect_final: Which basic move in your own work could you rehearse slowly, away from the real thing, before your next attempt?
pocket_idea: At Spartak even the top-ten player starts with a bouncing ball.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A top-ten player and a five-year-old start with the same ball bounce.
